leftEvidence.role: The mountain and those called blessed
leftEvidence.title: Persecution is joined to Kingdom and joy

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus calls people persecuted for righteousness and for his sake blessed.
points.right: Jesus recalls neighbor love and the saying to hate an enemy, then commands love, blessing, good, and prayer toward enemies and persecutors.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: He commands rejoicing because of heavenly reward and relates their treatment to earlier prophets.
points.right: The Father gives sun and rain to evil and good, and the hearers are called beyond reciprocal love toward perfection.

payload.posture: The blessing names hostility toward the hearers, and the later command directs their response toward hostile people.

rightEvidence.role: Law, righteousness, and the inner life
rightEvidence.title: Enemy love is grounded in the Father’s generosity

payload.tension: Being persecuted does not by itself prove righteousness; the sayings preserve “for righteousness” and “for my sake.”
payload.title: Persecuted people pray for persecutors
